results.title: ⛏️ GHANA IS LOOKING BEYOND GOLD 🇬🇭 Ghana is seeking fresh investment in manganese, iron and steel as it looks to expand its mining industry
results.description:
⛏️ GHANA IS LOOKING BEYOND GOLD 🇬🇭

Ghana is seeking fresh investment in manganese, iron and steel as it looks to expand its mining industry beyond gold.

A Chinese investment delegation has expressed interest in opportunities across the sector, including a possible equity stake in Adamus Resources. Meanwhile, Asanko Gold Ghana has outlined plans for open-pit expansion and underground mining.

The bigger opportunity here is value addition. Ghana has mineral resources, but the real economic gains come when more processing, industrial activity and skilled jobs are created locally.

Attracting investors is one thing. Turning that interest into actual projects, local industries and jobs is where the real test begins.

Can Ghana finally move beyond exporting raw minerals and build a stronger mineral-processing industry at home? 🇬🇭

#Ghana #Mining #CriticalMinerals

results.title: Speaking at the Financial Times (FT) Africa Summit 2026 in London, President John Dramani Mahama issued a direct message to Western investor
results.description:
Speaking at the Financial Times (FT) Africa Summit 2026 in London, President John Dramani Mahama issued a direct message to Western investors and global financial institutions, warning that hesitancy toward African markets will lead to missed economic opportunities.

In his address, President Mahama highlighted the rapid influx of capital from emerging global economies, emphasizing that Ghana and the broader continent maintain an open-door, non-aligned foreign policy welcoming trade and investment from the European Union, the United States, China, India, and Russia.

results.title: 🇬🇭🌍GHANA’S FOREIGN POLICY: FRIENDS TO ALL, ENEMIES TO NONE A VISION OF GLOBAL PARTNERSHIP AND ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITY President John Dramani Ma
results.description:
🇬🇭🌍GHANA’S FOREIGN POLICY: FRIENDS TO ALL, ENEMIES TO NONE A VISION OF GLOBAL PARTNERSHIP AND ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITY

President John Dramani Mahama has reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to an independent, inclusive, and forward-looking foreign policy anchored in a powerful principle: “We are friends to all and enemies to none.”

In his remarks, the President underscored Ghana’s openness to investors from every nation, emphasizing the importance of international cooperation, healthy competition, and mutually beneficial partnerships, including with global powers such as China and Russia.

The position reflects Ghana’s longstanding tradition of non-alignment and recalls the vision of Osagyefo Dr. Kwame Nkrumah, who advocated a foreign policy independent of the competing power blocs of East and West.

At a time of shifting global alliances and economic realignments, Ghana’s message is clear: national interest must remain at the heart of international engagement. By building bridges across geopolitical divides, Ghana can pursue investment, strengthen diplomatic relations, expand economic opportunities, and safeguard its sovereignty.

A nation that engages the world with confidence, welcomes partnership without surrendering its independence, and places its people's interests first can turn diplomacy into an instrument of lasting progress.
